topic: Passive advanced (be said to, have/get sth done)

questions.explanation: After 'is said', use the to-infinitive for reported belief.
'Have something done' uses the past participle.
Use the perfect infinitive after 'are believed' for a past action.

options: She got cut her hair yesterday.
She got her hair cut yesterday.
She got her hair to cut yesterday.
She got her hair cutting yesterday.
questions.explanation: 'Get something done' uses the past participle.

questions.q: The thief is thought ___ the country.
questions.explanation: A past escape after 'is thought' needs the perfect infinitive.

questions.q: We need to get the roof ___.
questions.explanation: 'Get something done' takes the past participle.
After 'is expected', use the to-infinitive.

options: I'll have tested my eyes tomorrow.
I'll have my eyes to test tomorrow.
I'll have my eyes tested tomorrow.
I'll have my eyes testing tomorrow.
questions.explanation: 'Have something done' arranges a service with the past participle.
'Was reported' is followed by the to-infinitive.
'Get something done' uses the past participle.

questions.q: The painting is said ___ stolen in 1990.
questions.explanation: A past passive event needs the perfect passive infinitive.

options: She had her house painted last month.
She had painted her house last month.
She had her house to paint last month.
She had her house painting last month.
questions.explanation: 'Have something done' means someone else did it for you.

questions.q: We are supposed ___ the report by Friday.
questions.explanation: 'Be supposed to' is followed by the infinitive.

questions.q: He got his suit ___ for the wedding.
questions.explanation: 'Get something done' takes the past participle.

options: The president is expected arriving at noon.
The president is expected to arrive at noon.
The president is expected arrive at noon.
The president expects to arrive at noon.
questions.explanation: 'Is expected' reports what people think will happen.

questions.q: They are said ___ in Paris now.
questions.explanation: An ongoing situation needs the continuous infinitive after 'are said'.
'Have something done' uses the past participle.

options: I must get my bike fixed — the brakes don't work.
I must get fixed my bike — the brakes don't work.
I must get my bike to fix — the brakes don't work.
I must get my bike fixing — the brakes don't work.
questions.explanation: 'Get something done' arranges for someone else to do it.
A current rumour about an ongoing action uses the continuous infinitive.

options: He had stolen his wallet on the bus.
He had his wallet to steal on the bus.
He had his wallet stolen on the bus.
He had his wallet stealing on the bus.
questions.explanation: 'Have something done' can describe an unpleasant thing that happened to you.
